2. CRITICAL SECRET POLICY
AUTH_SECRET IS NOT CLERK_SECRET_KEY

Treat these as completely separate credentials.

AUTH_SECRET belongs to Affiliate OS itself.

Clerk credentials such as:

CLERK_SECRET_KEY
Clerk client credentials

belong to the external Clerk authentication provider.

NEVER use a Clerk secret as AUTH_SECRET.

Do not substitute one for another.

3. AUTH_SECRET PROVISIONING

Generate a NEW cryptographically secure random AUTH_SECRET.

Preferred approach:

Generate it inside the secure execution/infrastructure environment.
Or generate it directly through the Cloudflare secret-management mechanism if supported.
Store it only as an encrypted Cloudflare Pages production secret.

The secret MUST NOT be:

pasted into chat;
printed in terminal output;
printed in logs;
placed into GitHub;
committed to Git;
added to README;
added to .env;
added to .env.example;
written into source code;
included in screenshots;
included in the final report;
echoed back to the user.

When verifying it, verify only:

AUTH_SECRET configured = YES

Never reveal its value.

4. ABSOLUTE NO-CREDENTIAL-UPLOAD RULE

Do NOT ask the user to upload credential files merely to provision AUTH_SECRET.

Do NOT create or commit:

credential files;
secret files;
.env;
.dev.vars;
API-key dumps;
JSON credential files;
copied Clerk credentials;
copied Neon API keys;
copied OpenAI keys;
copied Serper keys.

Existing secret files must remain outside Git.

If a secure secret cannot be provisioned through the available environment:

STOP WITH STATUS = BLOCKED.

Do not work around the security requirement.

Do not use a fake secret.

Do not use a placeholder secret.

Do not reuse another provider's secret.

affiliate-os
